title: Discrete modules with continuous action have functorial injective embeddings
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group and $A$ a finite ring. In the category $\mathcal C$ of left $A$-modules with a $G$-action by $A$-linear automorphisms such that every element has open stabilizer, with $A$-linear $G$-equivariant maps, there is a functor $J:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ and a natural transformation $j:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}\to J$ such that each $j_M:M\to J(M)$ is a monomorphism and $J(M)$ is injective. Consequently every object of $\mathcal C$ embeds in an injective object, so $\mathcal C$ has enough injectives in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Tag 04JF, label lemma-G-modules: functorial injective embeddings in Mod_{R,G}; the specialization to discrete G-modules

proof.text: A profinite group is a topological group and a finite ring is a ring, so [lem-exc-rg-discrete-modules-functorial-injective-embeddings] applies with $(G,R)=(G,A)$; its category of left $R$-modules with $R$-linear $G$-action whose elements have open stabilizers, with $R$-linear $G$-equivariant maps, is then exactly $\mathcal C$. It gives a functor $J:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ and a natural transformation $j:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}\to J$ with every $j_M$ a monomorphism and every $J(M)$ injective in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 04JF, label lemma-G-modules: the functorial embedding and its open-stabilizer specialization

proof.text: For each object $M$ of $\mathcal C$, the component $j_M$ of step 1 is a monomorphism into $J(M)$, which is an injective object of $\mathcal C$ in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Thus every object of $\mathcal C$ admits a monomorphism into an injective object, which is what it means for $\mathcal C$ to have enough injectives (the notion presupposed in [def-sp-injective-resolutions]).
